paragraphs: Okay, friend, deep breath. That was a heavy one, and it's heavy on purpose. God uses a hard picture here because He wants His people to see how serious it is to walk away from Him. The two sisters were His. God says, "They became Mine" (Ezekiel 23:4). Then they went chasing other lovers anyway, and the lovers they chased ended up being the ones who hurt them (Ezekiel 23:9, 22).

Here's the part that gets me. Oholibah saw what happened to her sister Oholah, and she kept going anyway. God says she "was more depraved than her sister" (Ezekiel 23:11). Seeing a warning and shrugging it off is something people do all the time. I once looked at a cookie tray that smelled like smoke and said, "I'm sure it's fine." It was not fine, friend. It was never fine. The sad part is that Oholibah's lovers were never going to stay loyal to her. God says what was behind it all: "you have forgotten Me and have cast Me behind your back" (Ezekiel 23:35).

So what does that mean for you? Whatever you lean on in place of God will not hold you up. God's word is a fair warning, and fair warnings are a kindness. Pay attention to the ones you've been given, and keep God in front of you instead of behind your back. And stay close, baker, because this word about the two sisters isn't finished yet.
